sets.title: Mock B · Paper 1
sets.desc: Real CFA Institute Level II Mock B, Session 1: vignettes and questions as published (44 questions, 2 h 12 min).

vignettes.body:
Pinku Singh is the chief financial officer (CFO) of Axiom, a publicly traded conglomerate that is split into three divisions. Singh wants to optimize the corporate and financing structure of the company and begins by determining which division has the lowest cost of capital based on the asset profiles presented in Exhibit 1.

Exhibit 1
# | Division A | Division B | Division C
Nature of assets | Mostly tangible | Mostly tangible | Mostly intangible
Fungibility of assets | Non-fungible | Fungible | Non-fungible

Singh employs the build-up approach to estimate the specific-company risk premium (SCRP) for Axiom. The firm's cost of equity is 13.5%. Singh estimates the market equity risk premium to be 7.0%, the industry risk premium to be 0.0% and the size premium for Axiom to be 1.2%. The risk-free rate is 3.0% and Axiom has a beta of 1.5.

Singh would like to take advantage of the under-leveraged balance sheet of Axiom while ensuring that the company's current shareholders retain control. Singh considers what corporate actions could achieve these objectives.

Division B generated an EBITDA of $10.8 million last year and is valued at 6.0x EV/EBITDA. Division B has two segments:
A wholesale segment which contributed 20% to the division's EBITDA. Comparable wholesale retailers are valued at 7.0x EV/EBITDA.
A consumer segment which contributed 80% to the division's EBITDA. Comparable consumer retailers are valued at 5.1x EV/EBITDA.

Singh evaluates if spinning off Division B's wholesale segment would have a material impact on shareholder value, which she defines as a change in shareholder value of greater than 5%.

questions.q: Based on their asset profiles, which of Axiom's divisions most likely has the lowest cost of capital?
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Division A's assets are mostly tangible but non-fungible, so on fungibility alone its cost of capital is expected to be higher than Division B's.
B. Correct. Division B's assets are mostly tangible and fungible. Tangible assets can be pledged as collateral and fungible, liquid assets give access to cheaper capital, so Division B has the lowest cost of capital.
C. Incorrect. Division C's assets are mostly intangible and non-fungible, so its cost of capital is expected to be higher than Division A's and Division B's.

questions.q: Based on the build-up approach, the SCRP for Axiom is:
questions.why:
A. Correct. re = rf + ERP + SP + SCRP, so SCRP = 13.5% − (3.0% + 7.0% + 1.2%) = 2.3%.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect: SCRP is wrongly calculated as re − Beta × ERP = 13.5% − 1.5 × 7.0% = 3.0%.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect: the size premium is missing: SCRP = 13.5% − (3.0% + 7.0%) = 3.5%.

questions.q: Which of the following corporate actions would best meet Singh's objectives?
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. A reorganization is a court-supervised restructuring of an insolvent company. Axiom is under-leveraged and Singh wants to add debt, so this does not fit.
B. Incorrect. An LBO is an acquirer-led strategy that uses a lot of debt to buy a target. Singh wants the current shareholders to keep control, so this does not fit.
C. Correct. A dividend recapitalization restructures the mix from equity to debt through debt-financed dividends or repurchases. It replaces expensive equity with cheaper debt, does not dilute shareholders' stakes and can increase value to shareholders.

questions.q: Based on Singh's analysis, spinning off the wholesale segment for Division B would lead to:
options: a material decrease in shareholder wealth.
no material impact on shareholder wealth.
a material increase in shareholder wealth.
questions.why:
A. Correct. Sum of the parts: 7.0 × 20% × 10.8 = 15.120 and 5.1 × 80% × 10.8 = 44.064, total 59.184. Division B is valued at 6 × 10.8 = 64.800, so the change is (59.184 − 64.800)/64.800 = −8.7%, a material decrease (the market values synergies between the segments).
B. Incorrect. Incorrect: this averages the two multiples ((7.0 + 5.1)/2 = 6.05), giving 65.340 and a change of only +0.8%.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect: this swaps the multiples (5.1 × 20% × 10.8 + 7.0 × 80% × 10.8 = 71.496), giving +10.3%.

vignettes.body:
Jules Clerc is an equity analyst at an asset management firm. Clerc is evaluating Lonza Credit Inc., a bank that prepares its financial statements under IFRS and has a 31 December year end. The bank is subject to the Basel III regulatory framework.

Lonza offers a defined benefit pension plan to its employees. To evaluate the pension plan, Clerc uses the data (in EUR millions) for the most recent year in Exhibit 1.

Exhibit 1
Benefit obligations at beginning of year | 1,415
Benefit obligations at end of year | 1,440
Fair value of plan assets at beginning of year | 1,470
Fair value of plan assets at end of year | 1,480

Based on the data from Exhibit 1, Clerc calculates the pension plan's funded status for the most recent year as part of her valuation of Lonza.

On 1 January of the current year, Lonza granted 4 million stock options to employees. The options vest 3 years after the grant date and expire 6 years after the grant date. The fair value per option was EUR 1.8 on the grant date.

Lonza is planning to issue 5 million restricted stock units (RSUs) to its employees. The RSUs will vest two years after issuance. Clerc uses a profitability measure – free cash flow as a percentage of revenues – to analyze Lonza. He considers how this measure would be affected immediately after the issuance of the RSUs.

Clerc uses the CAMELS (capital adequacy, asset quality, management, earnings, liquidity, and sensitivity) approach to evaluate Lonza. Clerc gathers Lonza's liquidity ratios over the past two years in Exhibit 2.

Exhibit 2
# | Most Recent Year | Prior Year
Liquidity Coverage Ratio | 95% | 110%
Net Stable Funding Ratio | 95% | 90%

questions.q: What is the funded status of Lonza's pension plan at the end of the most recent year?
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect: this is the change in funded status during the year: 40 − 55 = −15.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect: this is the increase in plan assets during the year (1,480 − 1,470 = 10).
C. Correct. Funded status = fair value of plan assets − benefit obligations = 1,480 − 1,440 = EUR 40 million overfunded.

questions.q: For the current year, Lonza's compensation expense related to its stock options will be:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect: this divides the total fair value by the 6-year term to expiry instead of the vesting period.
B. Correct. Expense = (4 million × EUR 1.8) / 3-year vesting period = EUR 2.4 million.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect: this recognizes the whole grant-date fair value in one year, without spreading it over the vesting period.

questions.q: After the issuance of Lonza's RSUs, the profitability measure used by Clerc would:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect: the RSU issuance is a non-cash event, so it would only decrease if it were treated as a cash event.
B. Correct. The issuance has no effect on cash flows or revenues, so free cash flow to revenue is unchanged.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect: neither free cash flow nor revenues are affected by the issuance.

questions.q: Based on Lonza's liquidity ratios at the end of the most recent year, which of the following is correct?
options: Lonza's Net Stable Funding Ratio has deteriorated from the prior year
Lonza's required stable funding is higher than its available stable funding
Lonza can withstand cash outflows 5% higher than its 30-day liquidity needs in a stress scenario
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect: a higher NSFR is an improvement and it rose from 90% to 95%.
B. Correct. NSFR = available stable funding / required stable funding. At 95% (below 100%), required stable funding is higher than available stable funding.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect: an LCR of 95% means Lonza can cover only 95% of its 30-day stress outflows, i.e. 5% less, not 5% more.

questions.q: Which of the following will Grap's backtesting model require?
options: Two iterations of the rolling-window procedure
A 13-month in-sample period for each rolling window
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect: rolling windows overlap (each has a 12-month in-sample period, 11 months of which overlap with the previous window).
B. Correct. One rolling-window iteration builds the factor portfolios and a second one over the same time span estimates the covariance matrix for risk parity weights, which avoids look-ahead bias.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect: the in-sample period is the previous 12 months (not 13) with a 1-month out-of-sample period.

questions.q: To mitigate survivorship bias, which method should Grap use when forming factor portfolios?
questions.why:
A. Correct. Point-in-time data: in each rolling window use only the companies that were in the index at that time (casualties as well as survivors).
B. Incorrect. Incorrect: only companies in the index at the end of the period are survivors, which creates survivorship bias.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect: only companies in the index for the entire 10 years are survivors, which creates survivorship bias.

questions.q: The annual 5% parametric VaR of the absolute return trading strategy is closest to:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect: this is the monthly VaR: −[0.5% − 1.65 × 7.1%] = 11.2%.
B. Correct. Annualize first: E(R) = 12 × 0.5% = 6.0% and σ = √12 × 7.1% = 24.6%. VaR = −[6.0% − 1.65 × 24.6%] = 34.6%.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect: this multiplies the monthly VaR by √12 (38.8%).

questions.q: For his complementary risk analysis, which of the following risk measures should Grap use?
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect: with a cash benchmark (zero volatility) relative VaR equals VaR, so it adds no information.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect: surplus at risk is for pension funds with liabilities, not for a hedge fund.
C. Correct. For an absolute return, equity market-neutral strategy, maximum drawdown (worst peak-to-trough decline) complements standard deviation and beta as a downside risk measure.

vignettes.body:
Julia Kassam is a portfolio manager who is reviewing public and private equity investments for her clients.

Erebor Limited
Kassam values a manufacturing company, Erebor, using the EV/EBIDTA ratio. The company's last reported EBIDTA is $90 million. Kassam collects relevant financial information (in $ millions) in Exhibit 1.

Exhibit 1
# | Debt | Common Stock | Preferred Stock | Cash and Cash Equivalents
Market Value | 880 | 550 | 210 | 375
Book Value | 630 | 280 | 270 | 375

Biotechnology Sector
One of Kassam's clients wants to increase their exposure to growth stocks in the biotechnology sector. The sector currently has a median P/E ratio of 10.7 and is expected to grow at 7%. Kassam uses the PEG ratio to identify overvalued stocks from her list of three selected biotechnology stocks in Exhibit 2.

Exhibit 2
# | Price per Share | Earnings per Share | Annual Growth Rate
Company A | $49.75 | $5.42 | 6.00%
Company B | $12.63 | $1.71 | 8.24%
Company C | $31.28 | $2.93 | 4.50%

Altair Corp.
Kassam evaluates the stock of Altair, which is a recently listed, high growth, biotechnology company. She is considering a stable market-based multiple to value the stock and does not want to make any adjustments to the reported financial statements. After reviewing recent analyst reports, Kassam notices that Altair has internally generated brands that are not shown as intangible assets on Altair's balance sheet. Further, she notes that certain discretionary accounting decisions about expenses have led to an inaccurate representation of Altair's economic performance.

Becq Inc.
Kassam values Becq, a small private company, using the excess earnings method. Relevant financial information is shown in Exhibit 3.

Exhibit 3
Fixed assets | $725,000
Working capital | $315,000
Last reported earnings | $191,290
Residual income growth rate | 2.50%
Required return on fixed assets | 8.50%
Required return on working capital | 3.25%
Discount rate | 11.25%

questions.q: Erebor's EV/EBIDTA ratio is closest to:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect: this uses book values (280 + 270 + 630 − 375 = 805; 805/90 = 8.9).
B. Correct. EV = market value of common + preferred + debt − cash = 550 + 210 + 880 − 375 = 1,265; 1,265/90 = 14.1.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect: cash is added instead of subtracted (2,015/90 = 22.4).

questions.q: Based on the PEG ratio, which company is overvalued compared to the industry?
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect: P/E 9.18 and PEG 1.53, equal to the sector median PEG of 1.53 (10.7/7): fairly valued.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect: P/E 7.39 and PEG 0.90, below 1.53: undervalued.
C. Correct. P/E 10.7 and PEG 10.7/4.50 = 2.37, above the sector median of 1.53: overvalued.

questions.q: Which of the following valuation ratios is most suitable for Kassam to value Altair?
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect: P/B misses internally generated intangibles such as brands, which are not on the balance sheet.
B. Correct. Sales are less subject to distortion or manipulation than EPS or book value and are more stable than EPS, so P/S is suitable without adjusting reported financials.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect: earnings are prone to manipulation through discretionary expense decisions and distort EPS.

questions.q: Based on Exhibit 3, the value of Becq using the excess earnings method is closest to:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect: this is only the value of the intangibles (1,399,008); tangible assets must be added.
B. Correct. Residual earnings = 191,290 − 315,000 × 3.25% − 725,000 × 8.50% = 119,427.50. Intangibles = 119,427.50 × 1.025/(11.25% − 2.50%) = 1,399,008. Total = 1,399,008 + 315,000 + 725,000 = about 2,440,000.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect: the required return on fixed assets (8.50%) is used as the capitalization rate instead of the discount rate.

vignettes.body:
Sandra Plessinger is evaluating several bonds for the fixed-income portfolios she manages.

She first considers the following 2-year, default-free bonds with embedded options:
Bond A is a 5% annual pay coupon bond and is callable at par ($100) at the end of year 1.
Bond B is a 5% annual pay coupon bond and is putable at par ($100) at the end of year 1.

To analyze these bonds, Plessinger creates a binomial interest rate tree using the rates in Exhibit 1, assuming an interest rate volatility of 20%, with branching from each node to a high state and a low state occurring with equal probability. Plessinger also considers the effective convexity of Bond B.

Exhibit 1 Binomial Interest Rate Tree (1-year rates)
# | Year 0 | Year 1 | Year 2
Upper node |  | 6.09% | 7.32%
Middle node | 2.00% |  | 4.91%
Lower node |  | 4.08% | 3.29%
Note: This exhibit was a binomial diagram in the original paper. Its figure was not in the pasted text: the Year 0 and Year 1 rates come from the answer explanations, the Year 2 nodes are reconstructed from them (4.08% × e^0.4 = 6.09%, 3.29% × e^0.4 = 4.91% and 3.29% × e^0.8 = 7.32%).

Plessinger next evaluates a 3-year maturity, callable investment-grade corporate bond. She computes an OAS of 51 bps using the same binomial interest rate tree in Exhibit 1. Plessinger considers the impact on the bond's OAS under a scenario where the bond's price is unchanged and interest rate volatility increases from 20% to 25%.

Finally, still using the binomial interest rate tree in Exhibit 1, Plessinger analyzes a 3-year, default-free capped floating rate bond with a par value of $100. The bond pays an annual coupon equal to the 1-year reference rate, is set in arrears, and is capped at 5.0%.

questions.q: Based on the binomial interest rate tree, the value of Bond A is closest to:
questions.why:
A. Correct. Work backwards: at 6.09% the value is 105/1.0609 = 98.97; at 4.08% it is 105/1.0408 = 100.88, which exceeds par so the bond is called at 100. Year 0: (100 + 5)/1.02 = 102.9412 and (98.97 + 5)/1.02 = 101.9339; the average is 102.44.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect: this ignores the call (uses 100.88 instead of 100): 102.87.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect: this treats the bond as putable instead of callable (103.37).

questions.q: The effective convexity of Bond B:
options: will become negative if the rate in Year 1 is less than the bond's coupon.
will become negative if the rate in Year 1 is greater than the bond's coupon.
questions.why:
A. Correct. An option-free bond has positive convexity and the put right reinforces it, so a putable bond's effective convexity cannot be negative (unlike a callable bond's).
B. Incorrect. Incorrect: if the Year 1 rate is below the coupon the bond trades at a premium, the put is not exercised and it behaves like a straight bond (positive convexity).
C. Incorrect. Incorrect: if the Year 1 rate is above the coupon the put is in the money and only provides a price floor.

questions.q: Under Plessinger's scenario, the OAS of the corporate bond will:
questions.why:
A. Correct. Higher volatility raises the value of the embedded call. With the price (and Z-spread) fixed, and Z-spread = OAS + option cost, the OAS must decline.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect: higher volatility decreases the OAS of a callable bond.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect: higher volatility decreases the OAS of a callable bond.

questions.q: The value of the capped floating rate bond analyzed by Plessinger is:
questions.why:
A. Correct. The cap of 5% binds when rates are above 5% (the 6.09% Year 1 rate and the 7.32% Year 2 rate), so there are paths where the floater's coupon is limited and its value is below par.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect: without the cap a floater sells at par on each reset date, but the cap binds on some paths in the tree even though the spot rates are below 5%.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect: a cap can only reduce the value of a floater.

vignettes.body:
Sophia Chang is the head of alternative investments at a defined benefit pension plan. Chang is considering an investment in liquid alternatives and identifies two requirements the investment must meet:
Requirement 1: Have a lower incentive fee than the industry average for traditional hedge funds
Requirement 2: Allow more frequent redemptions than traditional hedge funds

Chang is also evaluating hedge funds as potential additions to the portfolio. She identifies the following strategies and considers their returns, leverage, and liquidity:
Strategy 1: Multi-strategy funds
Strategy 2: Fund of funds
Strategy 3: Long/short equity funds

Chang identifies a skillful manager who deploys Strategy 3. She determines which of the following factors is likely the primary source of outperformance for this manager: market timing, stock selection, or use of leverage.

The pension plan has an objective to limit drawdowns. Chang considers what individual hedge fund strategy would best meet that objective when combined with the pension plan's stock and bond portfolio.

questions.q: Do liquid alternative investments most likely meet Chang's requirements?
options: No, they fail to meet Requirement 1
No, they fail to meet Requirement 2
questions.why:
A. Correct. Liquid alts are in most countries prohibited from charging an incentive fee and offer daily redemptions, so they meet both requirements.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect: liquid alts do not typically have incentive fees, so Requirement 1 is met.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect: liquid alts can be redeemed daily, more liquid than traditional hedge funds, so Requirement 2 is met.

questions.q: Compared to Strategy 2, Strategy 1 most likely has:
questions.why:
A. Correct. Multi-strategy funds have generally outperformed funds of funds, but with more variance and occasional large losses linked to higher leverage; flexibility and fast tactical allocation help.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect: multi-strategy funds use significantly more leverage than most funds of funds.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect: multi-strategy funds often impose investor-level or fund-level gates, unlike funds of funds.

questions.q: Which factor is most likely the primary source of outperformance for the Strategy 3 manager?
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect: most long/short managers are poor at portfolio-level market timing (they are too net long at highs or not net long enough at lows).
B. Correct. Stock selection defines manager skill for most long/short equity managers; market timing is an additive but secondary consideration.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect: leverage can be applied to increase positions, but stock selection defines skill (high leverage is used mostly by quantitative managers).

questions.q: Which of the following hedge fund strategies is best suited to meet the plan's drawdown objective?
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect: event-driven/distressed strategies show high maximum drawdowns when combined with a stock and bond portfolio and little risk reduction.
B. Correct. The opportunistic strategies (global macro, systematic futures, merger arbitrage, equity market-neutral) give the smallest maximum drawdowns when combined with a traditional portfolio and have low serial autocorrelation (good liquidity).
C. Incorrect. Incorrect: relative value/convertible arbitrage strategies show high maximum drawdowns and high standard deviations when combined.

vignettes.body:
Sebastian Moreno is an analyst at an asset management firm. He is analyzing the probabilities of default for bond issuers and the drivers of ROE for selected companies.

Moreno is tasked with a new project that looks to classify bond issuers based on their probability of default within the next 12 months. He gathers a large sample of financial and accounting metrics for 1,000 issuers and observes that the issuers are not linearly separable. He compares non-linear support vector machine (SVM), unconstrained classification and regression tree (CART), and SVM with soft margin classification. He wants to use a machine-learning algorithm that addresses non-linear separability and is not prone to overfitting.

Moreno also creates Model 1, a logistic regression model that uses two factors, profit margin (PROFIT) and leverage ratio (LEVER), to predict the probability of default. The binary dependent variable is 1 for companies that defaulted within the subsequent 12 months and 0 otherwise. Using the regression results in Exhibit 1, Moreno calculates the predicted probability of default for the average distressed company, which has PROFIT = –2.0 and LEVER = 3.0.

Exhibit 1
# | Coefficient
Intercept | –1.7878
PROFIT | –0.0185
LEVER | 0.3876

To analyze the drivers of ROE for software companies, Moreno collects fundamental data and compares two linear regression models. Model 2 uses profit margin (PROFIT) and interest coverage (COVER). Model 3 extends Model 2 by adding a third factor, the quick ratio (QUICK).
Model 2: ROEi = b0 + b1PROFITi + b2COVERi + εi
Model 3: ROEi = b0 + b1PROFITi + b2COVERi + b3QUICKi + εi

Moreno compares the R-squared and adjusted R-squared measures of the two models. The regression results for Model 3 are given in Exhibit 2.

Exhibit 2
# | Coefficient | t-Statistic | p-Value
Intercept | –1.4411 | –3.4888 | 0.0000
PROFIT | 0.4840 | 49.5319 | 0.0000
COVER | 0.7487 | 27.9215 | 0.0000
QUICK | 0.0919 | 1.9204 | 0.0558

Finally, Moreno wants to test if last-12-month sales (SALES) are a good predictor of ROE. He runs Model 4, which has the following specification:
Model 4: ROEi = b0 + b1SALESi + εi

A plot of the regression residuals against SALES is presented in Exhibit 3.

Exhibit 3
Note: Exhibit 3 was an image in the original paper (file KL3.png) and was not in the pasted text. From the answer explanation: in the plot of the Model 4 residuals against SALES, the variance of the residuals increases as SALES increase.

questions.q: Which of the following machine-learning algorithms is most suitable for Moreno's bond issuer classification model?
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect: non-linear SVM with more advanced boundaries reduces training misclassifications but is complex and prone to overfitting.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect: unconstrained CART can perfectly learn the training data and overfit unless regularization parameters are added.
C. Correct. SVM with soft margin classification adds a penalty for misclassified training observations and trades off a wider margin against total error, handling non-linear separability without overfitting.

questions.q: For the average distressed company, the probability of default predicted by Model 1 is closest to:
questions.why:
A. Correct. P = 1/[1 + exp(−(−1.7878 − 0.0185 × (−2.0) + 0.3876 × 3.0))] = 1/(1 + 1.8004) = 0.357, about 36%.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect: 0.56 is exp(b0 + b1PROFIT + b2LEVER) = exp(−0.5880), the odds, not the probability.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect: 77% omits the intercept.

questions.q: Compared to Model 2, Model 3 most likely has a:
options: lower R-squared and a higher adjusted R-squared.
higher R-squared and a lower adjusted R-squared.
higher R-squared and a higher adjusted R-squared.
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect: R² never decreases when a variable is added.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect: adjusted R² rises when the added coefficient's |t| > 1.0, and QUICK's t-statistic is 1.9204.
C. Correct. R² increases or stays the same when a variable is added, and adjusted R² increases if the new coefficient's |t-statistic| is above 1.0 (QUICK: 1.9204).

questions.q: The most appropriate conclusion to draw from the residual plot for Model 4 is that:
options: the model suffers from unconditional heteroskedasticity.
there is a non-linear relationship between ROE and SALES.
the F-test for the overall regression significance is unreliable.
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect: the residual variance increases with SALES, so it is correlated with an independent variable: conditional, not unconditional, heteroskedasticity.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect: a residual plot does not show the form of the relationship between target and feature.
C. Correct. With conditional heteroskedasticity the MSE is a biased estimator, so the F-test for overall significance is unreliable (and Type I errors rise).

vignettes.body:
Terry McCormick is a US-equity analyst working for a large wealth management firm. He is currently working on DCF valuations of various publicly traded firms, which report under the US GAAP.

Firm A
McCormick wants to identify the most appropriate approach to value Firm A, which consistently had positive FCFE during the past decade. Management is about to start an aggressive growth strategy primarily financed with debt. McCormick expects highly fluctuating amounts of net borrowing for the next three years. McCormick also expects annual earnings growth rate to fluctuate between 25% and 35% during the next three years before it gradually declines to long-run sustainable rate of 2%.

Firm B
McCormick calculates FCFE for the most recent fiscal year and gathers the selected financial information in Exhibit 1 (in $ millions).

Exhibit 1
CFO | 535
Investment in fixed capital | 110
Interest expense | 70
Net borrowing | 65
Tax rate | 30%

Firm C
McCormick reviews his FCFE valuation model for Firm C. Firm C's management has just announced that they will issue new common stock during the next year. McCormick evaluates the potential effect of this change on next year's FCFE forecast.

Firm D
McCormick estimates the intrinsic value of Firm E's common equity using the FCFF approach. McCormick calculates the present value of the firm's future FCFF as $800 million. McCormick estimates that $75 million of the firm's cash holdings is not necessary to generate operating cash flows. Current market values of the firm's debt and preferred stock are $250 million and $150 million respectively.

questions.q: Which of the following is the most appropriate approach to use for valuing Firm A?
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect: growth has three stages (high, declining, stable) and FCFF is preferred when the capital structure is changing.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect: FCFE is not appropriate when the capital structure is expected to change (fluctuating net borrowing).
C. Correct. Growth is 25%-35% for three years, then declines gradually to 2%: three stages. With highly fluctuating net borrowing (a changing capital structure) FCFF is preferred over FCFE.

questions.q: Firm B's FCFE (in $ millions) is closest to:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect: 425 = CFO − FCInv is an approximation of FCFF.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect: 474 is FCFF = CFO + interest × (1 − t) − FCInv = 535 + 49 − 110.
C. Correct. FCFE = CFO − FCInv + net borrowing = 535 − 110 + 65 = 490.

questions.q: Given Firm C's announced change, next year's FCFE forecast will most likely:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect: transactions between the company and its shareholders (dividends, repurchases, issuances) do not affect free cash flow.
B. Correct. Share issuances are a use of FCFE, not a determinant of it, so the forecast is unchanged.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect: share issuance does not affect free cash flow.

questions.q: The intrinsic value of Firm D's equity based on FCFF approach is closest to:
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect: this leaves out the $75 million of non-operating cash.
B. Correct. Equity = value of operating assets + non-operating assets − debt − preferred stock = 800 + 75 − 250 − 150 = $475 million.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect: this leaves out both the non-operating assets and the preferred stock.

vignettes.body:
Martin Chu is a portfolio manager for actively managed, long-only fixed-income accounts.

Chu examines the potential impact of GDP growth and inflation on the yields of default-free government bonds in Countries A, B, and C. Chu uses her forecasts in Exhibit 1 to identify the bond market with the largest expected increase in real yields.

Exhibit 1
# Country | Forecast Change in Nominal GDP Growth Rate | Forecast Change in Inflation Rate
A | +50 bps | +10 bps
B | +65 bps | +30 bps
C | –40 bps | +12 bps

In Country D, the YTM of zero-coupon, inflation-protected government bonds is 0.8% for the 1-year maturity and 1.0% for the 2-year maturity. In the same market, the YTM of a 2-year zero-coupon nominal government bond is 3.0%. Chu calculates the expected 2-year average inflation rate in Country D.

Chu reviews a diversified US bond portfolio, Portfolio A. His objective is to determine which of the following three sectors' spreads can be expected to narrow the most if the economy recovers from a business downturn.
Sector A: Investment grade consumer cyclical
Sector B: Speculative grade consumer cyclical
Sector C: Speculative grade consumer noncyclical

For Portfolio B, in addition to the long-only constraint, the client proposes adding a second constraint specifying maximum overweights and underweights of 10% relative to the portfolio's benchmark. Chu and the client discuss whether this policy change would impact the portfolio's optimal level of active risk.

questions.q: Based on Chu's forecasts, which of the following bond markets should experience the largest increase in real yields?
questions.why:
A. Correct. Real GDP growth change = nominal − inflation: A: 50 − 10 = +40 bps, larger than B (+35 bps) and C (−52 bps). Higher real growth raises the real default-free rate.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect: B's real growth increase is 65 − 30 = 35 bps, smaller than A's; the larger nominal change is irrelevant.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect: C's real growth falls by 52 bps, implying a lower real rate.

questions.q: The expected 2-year average inflation rate in Country D is most likely:
questions.why:
A. Correct. Breakeven inflation (3% − 1% = 2%) includes a positive inflation uncertainty risk premium, so expected average inflation is below 2%.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect: 2% ignores the positive inflation uncertainty premium and is too high.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect: expected inflation is below the breakeven (using the 0.9% average of the real yields would give 2.1%, a mistake).

questions.q: For Portfolio A, which of the following sectors most likely satisfies Chu's objective concerning credit spreads?
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect: investment grade cyclical spreads narrow less than speculative grade cyclical spreads.
B. Correct. Sector B is both speculative grade and cyclical, so it is the most sensitive to an improving economy and its spreads narrow the most.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect: noncyclical issuers are less sensitive to the business cycle than cyclical issuers.

questions.q: If the client's proposal regarding Portfolio B's constraints is implemented, the portfolio's optimal level of active risk would most likely:
questions.why:
A. Correct. The extra constraint lowers the transfer coefficient and so the expected information ratio. Optimal active risk σA = TC × (IR*/SRB) × σB falls.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect: the reduced TC would have to be offset by a proportional increase in IR, but skill is constant.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect: the constraint reduces the TC and so lowers the optimal active risk.

vignettes.body:
Theodore Silva, CFA, manages equity funds at Tritium Asset Management, which recently adopted the Standards. Silva is reviewing some of the firm's policies and procedures to determine if they are in compliance with the Standards.

Silva has a referral arrangement with Sterling Group, a large brokerage and research firm. In return for referring institutional clients to Silva, Sterling Group is allowed to advertise at Tritium's annual equity conference without paying a fee. Silva does not disclose this arrangement to referred clients because he does not pay Sterling Group for any referrals. Silva directs trade execution to Sterling for the referred clients because Sterling is an approved broker that provides best execution. Silva does not use Sterling's research.

Silva conducts due diligence on a mid-cap packaging company whose stock is actively traded. He determines the company's fundamentals are strong and buys its stock for one of the equity funds he manages. Silva provides commentary on the company's prospects in his monthly client newsletter. Silva has owned the company's stock in his personal portfolio for many years and has disclosed this in the fund's communications to clients. A few weeks after releasing the newsletter, Silva sells some of his personal position in the stock as part of rebalancing his personal portfolio. He earns a substantial profit from this sale.

Silva plays golf with the chief financial officer (CFO) of a small fintech company, RizenPay. During the round of golf, the CFO tells Silva that the last few weeks have been very busy for him. He adds that the company is growing fast and doing well financially. The next day, Silva purchases the latest fintech report prepared by an industry expert. The report is not available publicly and can only be purchased for a fee. The report is well-researched and projects that RizenPay will take market share from its competitors. A day later, Silva buys RizenPay stock for his funds.

Tritium's recommended policy for record retention is to maintain records of investment actions and client communications in electronic format. Silva is accustomed to retaining all of his and his clients' relevant files in hard copy form. He does not store any of the records in electronic format. He saves his records for 5 years, after which they are destroyed. Local regulations require record retention for 5 years.

questions.q: Does Silva violate the Standards in his dealings with Sterling Group?
options: Yes, by not disclosing the conference arrangement with Sterling to clients
Yes, by using Sterling's brokerage for trade execution without using its other services
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect: Silva violates Standard VI(C) Referral Fees by not disclosing the arrangement.
B. Correct. Standard VI(C): even without a cash payment, Silva and Tritium benefit from the referrals and give Sterling something of monetary value (free advertising at the conference), so the arrangement must be disclosed to clients.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect: the Standards require best execution but do not require using a broker's research; Sterling is an approved broker with best execution.

questions.q: Did Silva violate the Standards when selling his personal stake in the packaging company?
options: Yes, because he sold the shares at a profit
Yes, by acting against his own recommendation
questions.why:
A. Correct. Standard VI(B) Priority of Transactions: client transactions have priority. The fund bought first and selling an actively traded stock from his personal portfolio did not disadvantage clients.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect: a profit is not a violation as long as clients are not disadvantaged.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect: the Standard does not prohibit personal transactions that differ from current recommendations as long as clients are not disadvantaged.

questions.q: Did Silva violate the Standard relating to material nonpublic information by buying RizenPay's stock?
options: Yes, by trading on the information shared by the CFO
Yes, by trading on the information shared in the industry report
questions.why:
A. Correct. The CFO's comments were nonpublic but not material, and Silva used the mosaic theory, combining them with a report anyone can buy; no violation of Standard II(A).
B. Incorrect. Incorrect: the CFO's information was not material and Silva did not trade solely on it.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect: the industry report is available to anyone who pays and is not material nonpublic information.

questions.q: Does Silva violate the Standards with respect to record retention?
options: Yes, because of the format in which the records are kept
Yes, because records must be retained for a minimum period of 7 years
questions.why:
A. Correct. Standard V(C): records may be kept in hard copy or electronic form, and following the regulatory requirement (5 years) satisfies the Standard; 7 years applies only absent regulation or firm policy.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect: the Standard does not require a specific format.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect: the 7-year recommendation applies only if there is no regulatory requirement; the local rule is 5 years.

vignettes.body:
Owen Murphy, CFA, is a sell-side analyst covering the technology industry for Crozet Investments, a financial advisory firm. He prepares a research report on Company A and gathers forecasts from multiple external data providers. Murphy combines this information with a quantitative model developed by Jane Jones while she was an analyst at Crozet. Jones is no longer with Crozet.

Sharon Gaskill, CFA, is the CEO of Company B, a small, publicly traded fintech firm. Crozet Investments has recently initiated coverage of Company B, and Murphy has been assigned as the analyst. In an effort to increase attention to Company B, Gaskill participates in several interviews with the local press and accepts speaking engagements at industry conferences. Investors who hear her enthusiasm are convinced that Company B offers promising growth, and they buy shares of it. The increased demand for the shares leads to an increase in Company B's share price.

Crozet Investments is located in a city where many movies are filmed. Several famous actors are clients of James Bass, CFA, one of Crozet's financial advisors. At a family picnic, Bass describes the profile of his current clients as high-net-worth individuals in the movie business. One of the family members recalls a story about an actor who filed for bankruptcy. Bass confirms this actor is a former client.

Murphy's supervisor manages a large research department and, as a result, is not able to personally evaluate the conduct of all the employees in the department. The supervisor hires a deputy manager to oversee several employees and ensures the deputy manager is properly trained. The supervisor establishes the following policies to assist with compliance:
Policy 1: A monetary incentive will be offered as a reward for ethical behavior.
Policy 2: The deputy manager will be responsible for evaluating the ethical conduct of department members.

questions.q: To comply with the Standards in his research on Company A, Murphy must cite:
options: both Jones and the data providers.
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect: Standard I(C): research and models developed while employed by a firm are the firm's property, so Jones need not be cited.
B. Correct. Murphy must cite the data providers (sources of forecasts must be revealed under Standard I(C) Misrepresentation) but need not cite Jones, whose model is Crozet's property.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect: citing Jones is not required because her work belongs to the firm.

questions.q: Does Gaskill violate the Standard relating to market manipulation with her interviews and speaking engagements?
options: Yes, by engaging in information-based manipulation
Yes, by engaging in transaction-based manipulation
questions.why:
A. Correct. Standard II(B): there is no evidence that she spreads false information or that trades are intended to distort prices; intent is critical.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect: manipulation requires false or misleading information, and there is no evidence of that.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect: there is no evidence of trades intended to distort market prices.

questions.q: Does Bass violate the Standard relating to preservation of confidentiality at the family picnic?
options: Yes, in relation to his former client only
Yes, in relation to both his current clients and his former client
questions.why:
A. Incorrect. Incorrect: Standard III(E) also protects former clients, so naming the actor who is a former client is a violation.
B. Correct. Bass confirmed the identity of a former client, and confidentiality continues after the relationship ends. Describing his current client profile in general terms is not a violation.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect: he did not name current clients or discuss their finances.

questions.q: Does Murphy's supervisor violate the Standards in his oversight of the department?
questions.why:
A. Correct. Standard IV(C): incentives (monetary or not) that reward ethical behavior are allowed and delegating supervisory duties in a large department is reasonable.
B. Incorrect. Incorrect: monetary incentives for ethical behavior do not violate the Standard.
C. Incorrect. Incorrect: delegating supervision to a properly trained deputy is not a violation.
